{{spoiler}} {{Infobox_location | image = Sun station.png | title = Sun Station | type = Satellite | gravity = 0.4g - 0.7g | location = [[Sun]] | inhabitants = None | database info = {{BL3|)}} |caption="Science compels us to explode the sun!"}} The '''Sun Station''' is an ancient [[Nomai]] station in an extremely close and rapid orbit around the [[Sun]]. == Description == The Sun Station is a satellite composed of two huge modules connected by a destroyed passageway. The station contains many gravity tiles so that its users can walk instead of free falling. Sun Station contains two inactive [[Nomai Statue|Nomai Statues]] and the corpse of [[Idaea]]. After not receiving a command for over ten minutes due to the death of the Nomai, the Sun Station went into sleep mode and has been offline for 281,042 years. Sun Station Walkway.png|Destroyed walkway leading to the main chamber Sun Station Entry room.png|Entry room leading down to the main room Sun Station Upper floor.png|Upper floor of the main chamber Sun Station Upper Statue.png|Inactive Nomai statue on the upper floor Sun Station Lower floor.png|Lower floor of the main chamber Sun Station Lower Statue.png|Inactive Nomai statue on the lower floor == Accessibility == [[File:Ash Twin Towers Sun Station.png|thumb|Sun Station warp tower on Ash Twin]] The primary method to access the Sun Station is revealed within the [[Sunless City]] on [[Ember Twin]].Sunless City Anglerfish Overlook district: Who’s been computing shuttle trajectories to the Sun Station? Don’t worry; the station is in such a low stellar orbit, we’ve constructed a different, safer way to travel there from Ash Twin. The Sun Station warp tower located on [[Ash Twin]] can be used to warp to the Sun Station. The second and much more dangerous method is manually landing the ship on the Sun Station, a challenging feat given the Sun’s immense gravity and the Sun Station’s rapid orbit. Gaining access to the warp pad inside the Sun Station Tower on the Ash Twin is rather tricky, as the player only has a small window of opportunity to get to it. Exactly 5 minutes into the loop, the sand will cross the Sun Tower and the accessible door will begin to become exposed after it passes (the side with a balcony, specifically; the other side's door that's connected to the bridge is damaged and inaccessible). Once the sand has cleared enough to walk through, go through the right side door and carefully navigate around the spiked plants to the other side where the zero-g elevator can be accessed. From here, stand on the middle of the warp pad until the Sun Station is in the center of it's viewport and it will activate. The Sun Station is destroyed 10.5 minutes into the loop, as it is engulfed by the Sun when it grows to become a red giant. There is also readable inside the Station that displays the countdown until collision and how much time is left until the sun goes supernova. == History == ===The Ash Twin Project=== After the Nomai discovered the possibility to send objects and information back in time through [[Warp Core|warp cores]], they quickly found out it required exponentially more energy the farther back in time they wanted to send it.RAMIE: We’ve learned the negative interval of time between departure and arrival can be increased by adding more energy to the warp core. Problematically, the energy required to extend the interval increases at an exponential rate. The only power source capable of producing enough power to send information 22 minutes into the past was the energy produced by a [[supernova]].Should we build the Sun Station to power the Ash Twin Project? RAMIE: I understand this proposal is unsettling, but the Sun Station must be built if we hope to complete the Ash Twin Project. After the conception of the [[Ash Twin Project]] which would send probe launch orders back in time to find the [[Eye of the Universe]], the Sun Station was thus designed to induce a supernova.YARROW: Pye and Idaea have worked hard on the Sun Station, and it at last is complete. If everything goes as planned, this structure will prompt the sun’s explosion, which will in turn supply the power the Ash Twin Project requires. [[File:Sun Station Firing mechanism.png|thumb|left|Sun Station's firing mechanism]] The Nomai's plan was to fire the Sun Station and cause the sun to go supernova.YARROW: We’re nearly ready to activate the Ash Twin Project! Here is what will happen: First, the Sun Station will receive the order to fire at the sun, prompting it to explode. The Ash Twin Project would then use the energy produced by this supernova to send the probe launch order and the probe data back in time by 22 minutes. This would make the [[Orbital Probe Cannon]] shoot a probe in a random direction.YARROW: Using the energy from the resulting supernova, the Ash Twin Project will send the order for the Orbital Probe Cannon to fire back in time by 22 minutes. 22 minutes after this, the Sun Station would again trigger a supernova to power the Ash Twin Project and start the loop from the beginning.YARROW: Exactly 22 minutes after these orders are received, the Sun Station will again trigger the supernova to send the probe data from this cannon launch back in time. Once the Eye of the Universe would be found, the Nomai would receive its coordinates 22 minutes before firing the Sun Station and would consequently cancel the destruction of the Sun.PRIVET: We are! The Probe Tracking Module is ready to record each launch’s flight trajectory and will automatically transmit all relevant data to you. PRIVET: Once the probe determines the location of the Eye of the universe, I’ll send an alert directly to you and Ramie.YARROW: In total, each cycle created by the Ash Twin Project will last precisely 22 minutes. We can end this cycle at will. ===Ethics=== [[File:sun_eye (2).png|thumb|Nomai mural depicting a Nomai holding scales with on one side the Sun and on the other side the Eye of the Universe]] The construction of the Sun Station was the only thing the Nomai did that caused division and debate among them. The debate on the ethics of the use of a device able to destroy the solar system can be seen behind the energy controls of the [[Sunless City]] and inside the Sun Station. [[Idaea]] firmly opposed building the Sun Station, while [[Pye]] saw no other way to generate enough energy.IDAEA: The potential annihilation of an entire star system is too severe a cost. We shouldn’t build the Sun Station, no matter how badly we want the knowledge that comes with it.PYE: Poke, I’m deeply honored. Idaea, I comprehend your position; however, if we aren’t all but certain the Sun Station will not cause destruction once we’ve built it, then I won’t support the station’s use.YARROW: Are there other ways to generate this level of power? PYE: Theoretically, yes. Practically, no. I can’t imagine discovering them in our lifetimes... Idaea and Pye ended up building the Sun Station together, but their arguments continued on the station itself, with Pye making jokes about the Sun and Idaea being appalled at her lack of ethics.YARROW: Some time has passed since I checked in with you, Pye. How are you and Idaea progressing with the Sun Station plans? PYE: Presently, my assessment is that our plan will either fail explosively or succeed explosively. IDAEA: Pye, you know I don’t find that funny.PYE: You lack a sense of humor. IDAEA: At least I don’t lack a sense of ethics! ===Outcome=== After firing it, it turned out that the Sun Station was unable to impact the Sun in any meaningful way and would never be able to trigger a supernova. PYE: It fired, Yarrow. But it failed. The sun barely responded; there were infinitesimally small surface-level changes, but they were barely visible, even to the third eye. PYE: The Sun Station is useless. It will never, and could never, cause the sun to explode. This left the Ash Twin Project without a power source.YARROW: These words are difficult to write: The Sun Station did not work. YARROW: However, this is the closest we have ever been. The Ash Twin Project is theoretically sound; we were only unable to power it. Perhaps there is another way. Before the Nomai could think of another way to power the project, they were all killed by the [[Ghost Matter]] erupting from the [[Interloper]].Eye of the Universe Observatory: The Nomai who came to our solar system were following a signal from the Eye of the universe. They perished when the Interloper arrived, bringing with it the deadly substance we called ghost matter that flooded the entire solar system almost instantly and without warning. Over two hundred thousand years later, having reached the end of its lifespan, the Sun goes supernova naturally and not from any interference from the Sun Station.Sun Station evacuation notice: Star has reached end of natural life cycle. Now approaching red giant stage. This finally powered the Ash Twin Project and started the Nomai's time loop. ==Texts and recordings== {| role="presentation" class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" | ===Inside station=== |- |System sleep mode (''dependent on in-game time'') 281,042 YEARS AGO: No user commands received for 10 minutes. I’d hoped our terrible work was finished. |} == Notes & Trivia == * The [[Achievements#Hotshot|''Hotshot'' achievement]] is rewarded for successfully entering the sun station without using the [[Hourglass Twins#Ash_Twin_Towers|warp tower]] on Ash Twin. ** Using the ship is highly recommended as the thrusters of the jetpack of the EVA suit are too weak for the maneuvers needed to work around the Station's high orbital velocity and the strong gravitational pull of the [[Sun]]. ** Once near the sun station, it is possible to lock-on the entrances and make it easier by matching velocity to "park" the ship, and safely jetpack to get inside. ** The Eject button on the ship may be useful for exiting the ship, as its artificial gravity behaves oddly near the sun. * The Sun Station was first added in the Alpha Demo, containing a [[Sun Station (Alpha)|secret message]]. ==References== [[Category:Locations]]
